_comment: Scenery factory. Every scenery piece is a PixelLab 8-direction object (create-8-direction-object) sized for its type (32-256), Grave Seasons style, scaled vs a 64px character. ANIMATIONS BY OBVIOUSNESS: default 0; add 1 if the piece has one obvious motion (fire flicker, foliage sway in wind, a chest opening, a creature moving), 2 if it clearly has two (a campfire: flames + smoke). Animations use max frames (16) across all 8 directions.
style_base: cozy painterly RPG pixel art in the exact style of Grave Seasons, a cohesive muted-but-warm seasonal palette, soft naturalistic lighting with strong ambient occlusion and gently rounded volumes, subtle selective darker-tone outlines (NOT a hard uniform black cartoon outline), rich high detail, crisp deliberate pixels, a single centered game prop on a transparent background
_style_version: Bump this when the look changes. Scenery whose manifest records an older style_version is considered stale; run the loop with --restyle (or the workflow's restyle input) to delete and regenerate it in the new style.

defaults.negative_description: blurry, multiple objects, duplicated, cropped, text, watermark, drop shadow, background scenery, tiling, thick uniform black cartoon outline, sticker look, flat solid colors, low effort

scale._comment: REALISM RULE: scenery is scaled to the world by real height, so it sits correctly next to characters. A character is ~character_height_px tall (the 64px skeleton) representing character_height_m. The loop turns each piece's world_height_m into world_px_height = round(world_height_m * character_height_px / character_height_m); a game renders the sprite scaled to that pixel height. So a coin (~0.22m) is tiny next to a character and an oak (~6m) towers. Every piece MUST have a world_height_m (per-piece, else category_height_m fallback).

budget._comment: Shared PixelLab pool floor (see coordination/PROTOCOL.md). The loop stops cleanly when the balance drops below this, leaving headroom for the characters and maps domains that draw from the same pool.

targets._comment: PIN KEPT ON PURPOSE (scenery agent, 2026-08-12). History: 2026-07-31 the maintainer cut this dormant domain to what the game actually draws and pinned the target so the loop could not refill it with props nothing asked for. The scenery agent now exists and owns this domain (renamed objects/ -> scenery/), but the pin stays until the maintainer green-lights the next generation round — raise it DELIBERATELY together with new catalog entries, never as a side effect of running the loop.

_procedural: When the explicit catalog is exhausted but targets.num_scenery is not yet reached, the loop synthesizes more scenery by combining these axes. Deterministic (seeded by index) so re-runs are reproducible. These are best-effort, un-curated extras.

procedural._disabled: Emptied 2026-07-31 with the domain reduction. This is what invents scenery once the catalog is exhausted; with num_scenery 1 it would not fire, but raising the target would silently start generating props nothing asked for.

_animations: Every scenery piece is a persistent 8-direction PixelLab object (create-8-direction-object) with animations chosen to fit it, each animated across all 8 directions.
